title.source: 七銀行憑什麼讓他行卡進超商？從66台起步｜品牌故事
title.text: How Seven Bank connected other banks’ cards to convenience stores: from 66 ATMs

description.source:
零售集團為顧客的ATM要求，為何成立一家銀行？從2001年金融廳預備牌照文件場面與東京首批66台機器，沿著他行卡接入、合作銀行畫面與收據、分行宣傳，再到遠端支援和現鈔管理，看七銀行如何經營一個店內入口。創立日期依公司近同期揭露與沿革，不冒稱獨立監管原件；2002、2005、2009調查與2010營運各守自己的年代。匿名概念插圖，不重建特定顧客或紙鈔交易。

description.text:
Why did a retail group establish a bank in response to customers’ ATM requests? From a provisional-license document scene at Japan’s Financial Services Agency in 2001 and Tokyo’s first 66 machines, follow card connections, partner-bank screens and receipts, branch promotion, remote support and cash management. See how Seven Bank runs an outlet inside a store. Foundation dates rely on near-contemporary company disclosures and its history, not independently obtained regulatory originals. The 2002 and 2005 records, the 2009 survey and 2010 operations retain their separate dates. Anonymous concept illustrations do not reconstruct any particular customer or banknote transaction.

首次ディスクロージャー誌
開業から約半年でATM設置2,000台突破

c19r1o02: 四月二十五日，它再取得銀行營業牌照；
五月七日，開始受理普通預金開戶。
c19r1o04: 又過了八天，本店舉行ATM啟用儀式；
照片裡的人站在紅緞帶前，身後就是機器。
c19r1o05: 開頭的六十六台，五月十五日在東京二
十三區的五十九個地點，開始運作。
c19r1o08: 集團原本代收水電等公共費用；
顧客接著希望，存提款、匯款也能在店裡辦。
c19r1o09: 你能在購物的地方繳費，
卻不等於能用自己的卡提款；那要再接上金融機構。
c19r1o10: 不過，一九九九年其他超商就已有銀行合作；
這個集團不是超商ATM的首創者。
c19r1o12: 公司把自家存戶的金融服務，
和供合作金融機構使用的ATM網路，放在同一張業務圖。
c19r1a01: 先把合作接起來，再讓顧客知道；
啟用當天的年表，就並列三和銀行合作。
c19r1a02: 六月，這張網向東京以外延伸；
與靜岡銀行合作時，也開始在靜岡縣服務。
c19r2a30: 六月十一日，銀行也把系統接上全銀網；
匯款服務的啟用，還要等下一步。
c19r1a06: 到七月十三日，機器已經超過一千台；
找得到入口的地點，隨著設置擴大。
c19r1a07: 設點擴大，店裡接觸的現金也不只提款；
店家一天收下的營業款，能不能存進去？
c19r1a25: 同年十二月，銀行開始替Seven-Eleven店
舖辦理營業款入金，先接住店舖的需要。
c19r1a27: 機器接了店家的存款，其他人帶銀行卡來，
還是得知道，自己能在這裡做什麼。
c19r2a31: 當時公司把ATM列為合作銀行的共同出張所；
那螢幕，要照哪家銀行的規格？
c19r2a32: 它還把這種合作寫成業務外包；另一家銀行，
不必把自己的機器一起搬進店裡。
c19r1a14: 各家可辦業務、時段和費用不同；那麼，
最後印出的收據，也得跟著卡片換嗎？
c19r1a15: 我原先只注意提款口，沒想到，
連最後印出的收據，也按合作銀行的規格顯示。
c19r1a19: 同一份報告還記下，合作方製作海報，
在分行張貼，幫忙推動機器的使用。
c19r1a21: 公司把廣告後認知提高、合作機構增加，
和不同批次機器的使用成長，放在一起比較。
c19r1a22: 它比較不同時期新設的機器，
說二〇〇二年二月那批，使用次數成長更明顯。
c19r2a33: 拿來相比的，是開業初期六月設下的機器；
公司看到的是不同批次的使用成長。
c19r1a23: 至於哪種卡能存、哪種卡只提款，
服務表另外分列，仍得看自己那家銀行。
c19r1e04: 機器旁的電話接到中心，那麼入出金的資料、
警備與監視，又各走各的嗎？
c19r1e05: 公司把這四種工作接成統一管理的網路，
全天監看，並把設備與線路做成雙重配置。
c19r2e30: 銀行還另設備援中心，為突發狀況預作準備；
店裡一台機器，連線之外也有支援。
c19r1e06: 我在這裡開始看懂，一台機器要有人持續接手；
服務一多，現鈔又該怎麼顧？
c19r2e31: 商家把錢存進來、個人把錢提出去，
現金的兩端，往後都得被這張網照顧。
c19r1e09: 公司後來回顧，二代把紙幣處理做得更快、
容量更大，改善操作與現金運送效率。
c19r1e11: 同年十月，IY銀行改名七銀行；公司說，
新名字要讓人更容易想到店內服務。
c19r1e12: 你可能會想，機器、招牌和宣傳都增加，
大家總該知道自己的卡能不能用了吧？
c19r1e14: 二〇一〇年報說，有些店客沒有使用，
是誤以為自己的卡不能用，或一定要付費。
c19r1e15: 他們誤會的是手裡的卡，或螢幕上的費用；
銀行又打算怎麼補上這個缺口？
c19r1e17: 銀行因此在報告裡提出，把店內資訊擺得更醒目，
並和合作機構一起告知。
c19r1e18: 這也讓我追到另一個問題：有些人以為要付費，
代表每次提款真的都要付嗎？
c19r1e19: 如果顧客看見的是免手續費，替他接銀行、
照顧機器的那筆帳，又落在哪裡？
c19r1t01: 那筆帳得分開看；二〇一〇年報的模型，
把顧客費用交給帳戶所屬銀行決定。
c19r1t03: 它可以按自己的策略，替顧客定價或給優惠；
那機器經營者，又向誰收費？
c19r1t04: 七銀行收的，則是合作金融機構付給它的ATM使用費，
兩個方向不能混成一筆。
c19r1t05: 顧客看到免費，不能直接推成機器經營者沒有收入；
但也不能反過來猜每筆收多少。
c19r1t06: 我覺得有意思的，是合作銀行也成了客戶：
它一邊照顧存戶，一邊購買這張網。
c19r1t11: 當時的模型圖，已列出五百五十五家合作金融機構，
並不只是銀行一家類型。
c19r1t12: 它們帶著不同的卡、服務和定價進來，
機器經營者承接的，也是一組組不同需求。
c19r1t14: 截至二〇一〇年三月底的一年，
ATM相關手續費收入，約八百五十三億日圓。
c19r1t16: 所以不能拿這個總數，替某次提款開收據，
更不能直接說一台機器賺多少。
c19r1t19: 要讓別人願意依靠，經營者不只得接得通，
還得安排接通之後誰一直照看。
c19r1t20: 你把卡插進店裡的機器，交易訊息走遠了；
留在眼前的鈔票，又該怎麼顧？
c19r1n03: 公司說，一邊停了，另一邊有能力接全部交易；
可是，機器的狀況又由誰來看？
c19r1n07: 我原先只想到壞了再修，卻漏了另一種暫停：
維護服務本身，會不會占用機器？
c19r1n08: 但它確實列出，缺鈔、故障、定期檢查，
甚至裝鈔補鈔，都可能讓服務暫停。
c19r1n13: 所以報告記下，銀行會逐台分析使用趨勢，
照每台機器被使用的方式管理。
c19r1n15: 我原本盯著補進去多少，
報告卻又把目光拉到附近店家：它們也有錢要存。
c19r1n17: 七銀行說，它讓附近超商與其他企業把營業款存進ATM，
c19r1n18: 這裡講的是整體管理辦法，
沒有說某家店存進去的那張紙鈔，立刻就交給下一位客人。
c19r1n19: 當時報告把每台每月補鈔頻率記為約一點七次；
這就代表每個點都完全一樣嗎？
c19r1n22: 這張網走到二〇一〇年，機器、
合作方與管理方式，也跟著服務範圍繼續調整。
c19r1n24: 仍得確認卡種與時段、銀行核准，
還要機器正常有鈔，不能只看店裡有沒有機器。
c19r1n27: 我的答案是：零售集團設立銀行，再把合作、
辨認、支援和現鈔管理，接成同一張網。
c19r1ct1: 留言告訴我，你用過哪一種店內服務，
是後來才發現，背後還接著別家公司？

lines.source: 你想在超商用別家銀行的卡領錢，背後這張網，從六十六台機器起步。
lines.text: You want cash from a convenience-store ATM with another bank’s card. This network began with 66 machines.

lines.source: 二〇〇一年四月六日，金融廳裡，一位西裝人士在桌旁拿著文件。
lines.text: On April 6, 2001, at Japan’s Financial Services Agency, a person in a suit holds a document beside a table.

lines.source: 圖說寫的是取得預備牌照；銀行卻還沒有成立。
lines.text: The caption says a provisional license was obtained. Yet the bank did not exist.

lines.source: 我先卡住了：這份文件，離你能插卡還有多遠？
lines.text: That stopped me: how far was this document from letting you insert a card?

lines.source: 銀行分行裡的一包面紙，會怎麼把客人帶向超商？
lines.text: How could a packet of tissues at a bank branch lead customers to a convenience store?

lines.source: 而機器裡的鈔票，真的是裝得越多越好嗎？
lines.text: And was loading more banknotes into a machine always better?

lines.source: 跟著七銀行，追一個店角的提款入口，如何接到別家銀行的卡。
lines.text: Follow Seven Bank as we trace how a cash outlet in a store corner connects to other banks’ cards.

lines.source: 等銀行辦好了，機器就能接待每一張卡嗎？
lines.text: Once the bank was established, could its machines serve every card?

lines.source: 拿到預備牌照，還不是拿到一台能用的機器；四天後，IY銀行才成立。
lines.text: A provisional license did not mean a working machine. IY Bank was established four days later.

lines.source: 四月二十五日，它再取得銀行營業牌照；五月七日，開始受理普通預金開戶。
lines.text: It obtained its banking license on April 25, then began accepting ordinary-deposit account applications on May 7.

lines.source: 銀行先開門，店裡的機器也同一天啟用嗎？
lines.text: The bank opened first. Did the store machines start that same day?

lines.source: 又過了八天，本店舉行ATM啟用儀式；照片裡的人站在紅緞帶前，身後就是機器。
lines.text: Eight days later, its head office held an ATM launch ceremony. People in the photo stand before a red ribbon, with machines behind them.

lines.source: 開頭的六十六台，五月十五日在東京二十三區的五十九個地點，開始運作。
lines.text: Those first 66 machines began operating on May 15 at 59 locations across Tokyo’s 23 wards.

lines.source: 我在這裡才看見，領牌照和放機器，是同一個計畫裡前後相接的工作。
lines.text: Only then did I see licensing and installing machines as successive jobs within one project.

lines.source: 公司首次揭露誌給的起點，是顧客的要求；顧客原本還想在店裡辦什麼？
lines.text: The company’s first disclosure report starts with customer requests. What else had customers wanted to do in stores?

lines.source: 集團原本代收水電等公共費用；顧客接著希望，存提款、匯款也能在店裡辦。
lines.text: The group already collected utility bills. Customers then wanted deposits, withdrawals and transfers in stores too.

lines.source: 你能在購物的地方繳費，卻不等於能用自己的卡提款；那要再接上金融機構。
lines.text: You could pay bills where you shopped, but that did not let you withdraw with your own card. Financial institutions still had to connect.

lines.source: 不過，一九九九年其他超商就已有銀行合作；這個集團不是超商ATM的首創者。
lines.text: Other convenience stores already had banking partnerships in 1999. This group did not invent convenience-store ATMs.

lines.source: 光是店裡多一台機器，還說不清銀行的工作；它要接待誰的客人？
lines.text: One more machine in a store does not explain a bank’s work. Whose customers would it serve?

lines.source: 公司把自家存戶的金融服務，和供合作金融機構使用的ATM網路，放在同一張業務圖。
lines.text: The company’s business diagram includes both services for its own depositors and an ATM network for partner financial institutions.

lines.source: 這條路，要從實際合作開始；啟用那天，哪家銀行也跟著接進來？
lines.text: That connection needed an actual partnership. Which bank joined when the machines launched?

lines.source: 先把合作接起來，再讓顧客知道；啟用當天的年表，就並列三和銀行合作。
lines.text: Connect the partners, then tell customers. The launch-day chronology also lists the partnership with Sanwa Bank.

lines.source: 六月，這張網向東京以外延伸；與靜岡銀行合作時，也開始在靜岡縣服務。
lines.text: In June, the network spread beyond Tokyo. The Shizuoka Bank partnership also brought service to Shizuoka Prefecture.

lines.source: 設點與合作往前走，新的卡片功能卻不是同一天全部打開。
lines.text: Locations and partnerships expanded, but new card functions did not all open on one day.

lines.source: 六月十一日，銀行也把系統接上全銀網；匯款服務的啟用，還要等下一步。
lines.text: On June 11, the bank also connected its system to the Zengin network. Transfer service still had another step to go.

lines.source: 六月十三日，都市銀行卡也能在這裡提款；那匯款，是不是同一天開始？
lines.text: On June 13, cards from city banks could also make withdrawals here. Did transfers start that day too?

lines.source: 匯款服務又到六月十八日才開始。
lines.text: Transfer service did not begin until June 18.

lines.source: 到七月十三日，機器已經超過一千台；找得到入口的地點，隨著設置擴大。
lines.text: By July 13, there were over 1,000 machines. Installation brought the service to more locations.

lines.source: 設點擴大，店裡接觸的現金也不只提款；店家一天收下的營業款，能不能存進去？
lines.text: As locations expanded, cash in stores meant more than withdrawals. Could stores deposit the day’s takings?

lines.source: 同年十二月，銀行開始替Seven-Eleven店舖辦理營業款入金，先接住店舖的需要。
lines.text: That December, the bank began handling sales-proceeds deposits for Seven-Eleven stores, addressing stores’ needs first.

lines.source: 機器接了店家的存款，其他人帶銀行卡來，還是得知道，自己能在這裡做什麼。
lines.text: Machines accepted stores’ deposits. Other people arriving with bank cards still needed to know what they could do here.

lines.source: 二〇〇二年揭露誌寫，ATM設點會揭示合作銀行的招牌，讓顧客辨認。
lines.text: The 2002 disclosure report says ATM locations displayed partner-bank signs so customers could identify them.

lines.source: 當時公司把ATM列為合作銀行的共同出張所；那螢幕，要照哪家銀行的規格？
lines.text: The company then described the ATMs as shared outposts of partner banks. Whose specifications would their screens follow?

lines.source: 它還把這種合作寫成業務外包；另一家銀行，不必把自己的機器一起搬進店裡。
lines.text: It also described this partnership as outsourcing. Another bank did not have to bring its own machines into the store.

lines.source: 如果你拿的是適用合作卡，機器的畫面，就按那家合作銀行的規格顯示。
lines.text: If you had an eligible partner card, the screen displayed information to that partner bank’s specifications.

lines.source: 各家可辦業務、時段和費用不同；那麼，最後印出的收據，也得跟著卡片換嗎？
lines.text: Services, hours and fees differed by institution. Would the final printed receipt also change with the card?

lines.source: 我原先只注意提款口，沒想到，連最後印出的收據，也按合作銀行的規格顯示。
lines.text: I had only noticed the cash outlet. I had not expected even the receipt to follow the partner bank’s specifications.

lines.source: 但收據要操作之後才看得到；客人還沒靠近機器前，誰先把消息送給他？
lines.text: But you only see a receipt after operating the machine. Who tells customers before they approach it?

lines.source: 店內先擺服務冊子、貼海報，銀行也和零售集團一起推廣ATM的用途。
lines.text: Stores displayed service leaflets and posters. The bank also promoted ATM uses with the retail group.

lines.source: 開頭那包面紙，就是合作金融機構製作、在自家分行發送的宣傳物。
lines.text: That opening packet of tissues was promotional material made by partner financial institutions and distributed at their branches.

lines.source: 同一份報告還記下，合作方製作海報，在分行張貼，幫忙推動機器的使用。
lines.text: The same report also records partners making posters and displaying them in branches to encourage ATM use.

lines.source: 那麼，公司報告裡，不同批次新設機器的使用次數，成長有什麼差別？
lines.text: So, in the company’s report, how did usage-count growth differ between newly installed machine cohorts?

lines.source: 公司把廣告後認知提高、合作機構增加，和不同批次機器的使用成長，放在一起比較。
lines.text: The company considered greater awareness after advertising and more partners alongside usage growth in different machine cohorts.

lines.source: 它比較不同時期新設的機器，說二〇〇二年二月那批，使用次數成長更明顯。
lines.text: Comparing installation periods, it said the February 2002 cohort showed more pronounced growth in usage counts.

lines.source: 拿來相比的，是開業初期六月設下的機器；公司看到的是不同批次的使用成長。
lines.text: The comparison group was installed in June, early in operations. The company was observing usage growth in different cohorts.

lines.source: 至於哪種卡能存、哪種卡只提款，服務表另外分列，仍得看自己那家銀行。
lines.text: Which cards allowed deposits, and which only withdrawals? The service table lists them separately; your own bank still matters.

lines.source: 服務往店裡集中，顧客真遇到不懂的步驟，總不能只問機殼；該找誰？
lines.text: Services gathered in stores, but a customer confused by a step could not just ask the casing. Who could help?

lines.source: 機殼旁就接了一條求助的路；二〇〇二年報告，已記下ATM附設電話。
lines.text: There was a way to seek help beside the casing. The 2002 report already records phones attached to ATMs.

lines.source: 使用者拿起話筒，詢問會送到監視中心，由那裡回應操作中的疑問。
lines.text: When users lifted the receiver, their inquiry reached the monitoring center, which answered operating questions.

lines.source: 你要問的不是貨架商品，接手的人也得能處理這台機器的服務。
lines.text: You were not asking about shelf products. Whoever answered also needed to handle this machine’s services.

lines.source: 機器旁的電話接到中心，那麼入出金的資料、警備與監視，又各走各的嗎？
lines.text: The machine’s phone reached the center. Did deposit and withdrawal data, security and monitoring each take separate paths?

lines.source: 公司把這四種工作接成統一管理的網路，全天監看，並把設備與線路做成雙重配置。
lines.text: The company linked these four jobs in one managed network, monitored around the clock, with duplicated equipment and lines.

lines.source: 銀行還另設備援中心，為突發狀況預作準備；店裡一台機器，連線之外也有支援。
lines.text: The bank also established a backup center for unexpected events. A store machine had support beyond its connection.

lines.source: 我在這裡開始看懂，一台機器要有人持續接手；服務一多，現鈔又該怎麼顧？
lines.text: Here I began to see that someone had to keep taking care of a machine. With more services, what about the cash?

lines.source: 機器接待的也不只個人；二〇〇三財年，營業款入金開始走向一般企業。
lines.text: The machines served more than individuals. In fiscal 2003, sales-proceeds deposits began extending to businesses generally.

lines.source: 商家把錢存進來、個人把錢提出去，現金的兩端，往後都得被這張網照顧。
lines.text: Businesses put money in; individuals took money out. This network would have to manage both sides of cash.

lines.source: 機器越設越多，銀行後來又從鈔票處理這一端，改了什麼？
lines.text: As more machines were installed, what did the bank later change in banknote handling?

lines.source: 二〇〇五年四月，設置台數超過一萬；七月，第二代ATM開始導入。
lines.text: In April 2005, installations exceeded 10,000. Second-generation ATMs began rolling out in July.

lines.source: 公司後來回顧，二代把紙幣處理做得更快、容量更大，改善操作與現金運送效率。
lines.text: Looking back, the company says the second generation handled notes faster and held more, improving operation and cash-transport efficiency.

lines.source: 同年十月，IY銀行改名七銀行；公司說，新名字要讓人更容易想到店內服務。
lines.text: That October, IY Bank became Seven Bank. The company said the new name should make the store service easier to recognize.

lines.source: 你可能會想，機器、招牌和宣傳都增加，大家總該知道自己的卡能不能用了吧？
lines.text: You might think more machines, signs and promotion would mean everyone knew whether their card worked.

lines.source: 可是二〇〇九年十一月的一次萬人調查，讓這件事又出現一個缺口。
lines.text: But a survey of 10,000 people in November 2009 exposed another gap.

lines.source: 二〇一〇年報說，有些店客沒有使用，是誤以為自己的卡不能用，或一定要付費。
lines.text: The 2010 annual report says some store customers did not use ATMs because they wrongly thought their cards were unsupported or fees were unavoidable.

lines.source: 他們誤會的是手裡的卡，或螢幕上的費用；銀行又打算怎麼補上這個缺口？
lines.text: They misunderstood their card or the fees on the screen. How did the bank plan to close that gap?

lines.source: 卡片接上了，人卻可能停在前面，根本沒有把它拿出來的打算。
lines.text: A card could be connected, yet its holder might stop short, never intending to take it out.

lines.source: 銀行因此在報告裡提出，把店內資訊擺得更醒目，並和合作機構一起告知。
lines.text: The bank therefore proposed more visible in-store information and joint communication with partner institutions in its report.

lines.source: 這也讓我追到另一個問題：有些人以為要付費，代表每次提款真的都要付嗎？
lines.text: That led me to another question: if some people expected a fee, did every withdrawal really cost one?

lines.source: 如果顧客看見的是免手續費，替他接銀行、照顧機器的那筆帳，又落在哪裡？
lines.text: If customers saw “no fee,” who paid for connecting their bank and keeping the machine running?

lines.source: 那筆帳得分開看；二〇一〇年報的模型，把顧客費用交給帳戶所屬銀行決定。
lines.text: Those bills must be separated. The 2010 annual report’s model leaves customer fees to the bank holding the account.

lines.source: 它可以按自己的策略，替顧客定價或給優惠；那機器經營者，又向誰收費？
lines.text: That bank could set prices or offer discounts under its own strategy. Who paid the machine operator?

lines.source: 七銀行收的，則是合作金融機構付給它的ATM使用費，兩個方向不能混成一筆。
lines.text: Seven Bank received ATM usage fees from partner financial institutions. These two payment flows must stay separate.

lines.source: 顧客看到免費，不能直接推成機器經營者沒有收入；但也不能反過來猜每筆收多少。
lines.text: Free service for customers does not directly mean no income for the operator. Nor can we guess the fee per transaction.

lines.source: 我覺得有意思的，是合作銀行也成了客戶：它一邊照顧存戶，一邊購買這張網。
lines.text: What interests me is that partner banks became customers too: serving depositors while buying access to this network.

lines.source: 報告把借用網路，和自己建一整套ATM來比較；合作方為什麼願意買？
lines.text: The report compares using the network with building an entire ATM system. Why would partners pay?

lines.source: 合作方可以把服務伸到這些設點，減少自有機器的維護與資金負擔。
lines.text: Partners could extend services to these locations while reducing the maintenance and funding burden of their own machines.

lines.source: 這樣的合作，當時接進了多少家金融機構？
lines.text: How many financial institutions had joined this arrangement then?

lines.source: 當時的模型圖，已列出五百五十五家合作金融機構，並不只是銀行一家類型。
lines.text: The model diagram already listed 555 partner financial institutions, not only banks.

lines.source: 它們帶著不同的卡、服務和定價進來，機器經營者承接的，也是一組組不同需求。
lines.text: They brought different cards, services and prices. The operator was taking on distinct sets of needs.

lines.source: 年報有一欄可以看；同一年度的帳上，這門工作究竟留下了多少收入？
lines.text: The annual report has a figure for that. How much revenue did this work generate in that reporting year?

lines.source: 截至二〇一〇年三月底的一年，ATM相關手續費收入，約八百五十三億日圓。
lines.text: For the year ending March 2010, ATM-related fee income was about 85.3 billion yen.

lines.source: 那是整張網一整年的收入，還沒把設點、資金與營運的各種支出扣完。
lines.text: That was a full year’s revenue for the whole network, before deducting all location, funding and operating expenses.

lines.source: 所以不能拿這個總數，替某次提款開收據，更不能直接說一台機器賺多少。
lines.text: We cannot use that total as a receipt for one withdrawal, still less call it one machine’s profit.

lines.source: 如果別人想把這張網當備援，出問題又由誰接手？
lines.text: If someone wanted this network as a backup, who would take over when a problem arose?

lines.source: 報告甚至把這張網，列為合作方原有ATM網路的備援選擇。
lines.text: The report even lists the network as a backup option for partners’ existing ATM networks.

lines.source: 要讓別人願意依靠，經營者不只得接得通，還得安排接通之後誰一直照看。
lines.text: To earn that reliance, the operator needed more than a connection: someone had to keep looking after it.

lines.source: 你把卡插進店裡的機器，交易訊息走遠了；留在眼前的鈔票，又該怎麼顧？
lines.text: You insert a card in a store machine, and transaction messages travel away. What about the banknotes still before you?

lines.source: 訊息先接到中繼；二〇一〇年報，記的是橫濱與大阪兩套系統。
lines.text: The messages first reach relay systems. The 2010 report records two, in Yokohama and Osaka.

lines.source: ATM和合作金融機構透過它們處理交易，兩邊平常都在運作。
lines.text: ATMs and partner institutions process transactions through them. Both normally operate.

lines.source: 公司說，一邊停了，另一邊有能力接全部交易；可是，機器的狀況又由誰來看？
lines.text: The company says either could handle all transactions if the other stopped. But who watched the machines’ condition?

lines.source: 同份年報記載，支援中心位於東京與大阪，全天待命。
lines.text: The same annual report locates support centers in Tokyo and Osaka, on call around the clock.

lines.source: 你聽到兩組城市，是因為中繼交易與支援現場，本來就是不同的工作。
lines.text: You hear two pairs of cities because relaying transactions and supporting sites are different jobs.

lines.source: 機器出了問題，中心先用遠端方式處理，必要時再協調警備或維修公司。
lines.text: If a machine has a problem, the center first handles it remotely, coordinating security or maintenance companies when needed.

lines.source: 我原先只想到壞了再修，卻漏了另一種暫停：維護服務本身，會不會占用機器？
lines.text: I had only thought of repairing breakdowns. I missed another pause: could maintenance itself occupy the machine?

lines.source: 但它確實列出，缺鈔、故障、定期檢查，甚至裝鈔補鈔，都可能讓服務暫停。
lines.text: The report does list cash shortages, failures, regular checks and even cash loading or replenishment as possible service interruptions.

lines.source: 那麼，乾脆一次裝很多鈔票，不就好了？
lines.text: Then why not just load lots of banknotes at once?

lines.source: 回到開頭那個問題：多放現金，能少補幾次，卻會讓資金成本上升。
lines.text: Back to the opening question: more cash can mean fewer refills, but higher funding costs.

lines.source: 少放一些，補鈔頻率又增加，相關的外包成本也跟著往上走。
lines.text: Less cash means more frequent refills, pushing up the related outsourcing costs.

lines.source: 你需要的是來的時候有鈔可領；營運者卻得處理兩種成本，不斷做取捨。
lines.text: You need cash when you arrive. The operator must keep balancing these two costs.

lines.source: 所以報告記下，銀行會逐台分析使用趨勢，照每台機器被使用的方式管理。
lines.text: The report therefore records the bank analyzing usage trends machine by machine and managing each according to how it is used.

lines.source: 逐台分析了使用趨勢，還有沒有別的現金入口，能跟提款需求一起管理？
lines.text: Beyond analyzing each machine, was there another cash inflow it could manage alongside withdrawal demand?

lines.source: 我原本盯著補進去多少，報告卻又把目光拉到附近店家：它們也有錢要存。
lines.text: I had focused on how much cash was replenished. The report turned to nearby stores: they also had money to deposit.

lines.source: 前面開始的營業款入金，到這時就跟整張網的現金管理接在一起。
lines.text: The sales-proceeds deposits introduced earlier had now become part of cash management across the network.

lines.source: 七銀行說，它讓附近超商與其他企業把營業款存進ATM，改善現金管理效率。
lines.text: Seven Bank says it enabled nearby convenience stores and other businesses to deposit takings at ATMs, improving cash-management efficiency.

lines.source: 這裡講的是整體管理辦法，沒有說某家店存進去的那張紙鈔，立刻就交給下一位客人。
lines.text: This describes overall management. It does not say a note deposited by one store immediately went to the next customer.

lines.source: 當時報告把每台每月補鈔頻率記為約一點七次；這就代表每個點都完全一樣嗎？
lines.text: The report then recorded about 1.7 refills per machine per month. Did that mean every location was identical?

lines.source: 這是當年網路平均的營運數字；不同機器的使用趨勢，仍然要分別照看。
lines.text: It was that year’s network-average operating figure. Different machines’ usage trends still needed individual attention.

lines.source: 這張網走到二〇一〇年，機器、合作方與管理方式，也跟著服務範圍繼續調整。
lines.text: By 2010, the machines, partners and management practices kept adjusting as the network’s service scope expanded.

lines.source: 這張網已經接上，那你手裡任何一張卡，現在走過去都能提款嗎？
lines.text: With this network connected, could you walk over now and withdraw using any card in your hand?

lines.source: 仍得確認卡種與時段、銀行核准，還要機器正常有鈔，不能只看店裡有沒有機器。
lines.text: You still needed the right card and hours, bank approval, and a working machine with cash. A machine’s presence alone was not enough.

lines.source: 回到開頭，店角那台機器，怎麼替別家銀行的客人辦事？
lines.text: Back to the opening: how did that store-corner machine serve other banks’ customers?

lines.source: 我的答案是：零售集團設立銀行，再把合作、辨認、支援和現鈔管理，接成同一張網。
lines.text: My answer: a retail group established a bank, then linked partnerships, identification, support and cash management into one network.

lines.source: 留言告訴我，你用過哪一種店內服務，是後來才發現，背後還接著別家公司？
lines.text: Tell me in the comments: which store service did you use before discovering another company was behind it?

lines.source: 想繼續拆開日用品背後，那些替你接住麻煩的生意，歡迎訂閱品牌故事。
lines.text: To keep exploring the businesses behind everyday things that handle hassles for you, subscribe to Brand Stories.
